It has been another crazy day for global financial markets and we just learned that President Trump is instituting a 90-day pause on tariffs. Wall Street loved the news and we are seeing just a huge rally in the stock market. We've been getting a ton of questions from WSJ subscribers about the rally today and the market moves over the past week. Let's dive into some of them. Now, we have a question here from Kimberly. Does today's jump in the stock market due to the pause in tariffs make sense [...] municipalities and could really dent their finances. Our next question is from Christian. Christian asks, "How likely is the Fed to step in to save markets?" The short answer is not very likely. In March 2020 and during the global financial crisis, the Fed quickly stepped in to save the financial markets. This time around, there's one big reason investors don't think the Fed will do the same, and that is inflation. Inflation has been a problem for everyday Americans for years, and the Fed is [...] But the past few days have been a really different story. And what we've seen is that a lot of investors have been hiding out in cash. assets in cash-like investments, money market funds, hit a record of more than $7 trillion recently. That's the highest in records going back to the 1970s. So, the short answer is that a lot of investors have been keeping their money in cash. Thank you guys so much for all of these questions. Please keep them coming on WSJ.com.
